newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-BASUKI BEATS YOUNG KOURNIKOVA IN FIRST ROUND.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BASUKI BEATS YOUNG KOURNIKOVA IN FIRST ROUND.

text.p: Indonesian Yayuk Basuki, a late entry in the $450,000 Advanta Championships, used her experience to beat young Russian Anna Kournikova 6-4 7-6 (7-1) in a first-round match on Tuesday.
Basuki, 25 years old and ranked 33rd in the world, was inserted into the draw only after Jennifer Capriati withdrew two days before the tournament started.
The 15-year-old Kournikova, the former world top-ranked junior player, began the year ranked 281st but is currently ranked 56th.
"I don't feel I played very well, but I have a little more experience than her," Basuki said. "She's young, and sometimes I don't think she can keep her emotions. But she has a great future."

Basuki held an early service break in the second set before Kournikova broke back to tie the set at 4-4. After holding serve in the next game, Kournikova held a set point at 4-5 on Basuki's serve but netted a backhand service return.

Basuki went on to hold serve. In the tiebreak, she double-faulted on the second point but won the next six points. She won on the first match point on a running forehand down the line with Kournikova at the net.
In the day's only match involving a seeded player, sixth-seeded, eighth-ranked Iva Majoli of Croatia defeated Judith Wiesner of Austria 6-2 6-2 in a first-round match.
Majoli got two early service breaks in each set to earn a second-round meeting with American Chanda Rubin.

In another first-round match, Lisa Raymond, who grew up in nearby Wayne, Pennsylvania, defeated fellow American Gigi Fernandez 6-1 3-6 6-3. The 35th-ranked Raymond, who won her first WTA Tour title last month in Quebec City, will face second seed Conchita Martinez of Spain in the second round.

Tenth-ranked Brenda Schultz-McCarthy of the Netherlands withdrew from the tournament Tuesday after aggravating a left thigh strain suffered last week at the Bank of the West Classic in Oakland. Her place in the draw will be taken by American Lori McNeil.
